title: Credit Attribution in Timestamped Soccer Networks Using Multivariate Hawkes Processes
abstract: arXiv:2610.12775v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The two main traditional player statistics used in soccer are goals scored and assists, with an assist credited when a player's pass immediately leads to a teammate scoring. Attributing credit solely to the player who makes the final pass before a goal fails to account for the contributions of multiple players in the buildup to the goal. Consequently, traditional statistics provide only a limited view of player involvement. In this paper, we use multivariate Hawkes processes (MHPs) to model timestamped sequences of passes and shots, which form continuous-time networks. MHPs provide a branching mechanism where an event (a pass or shot) can be generated as a child of a previous event, which allows us to quantify each pass's contribution to a subsequent pass or shot. translated_title: 使用多元霍克斯过程在带时间戳的足球网络中进行贡献归因
translated_abstract: 足球中两种主要的传统球员统计数据是进球和助攻，当一名球员的传球直接导致队友进球时，该球员获得助攻。然而，仅将功劳归于进球前最后一次传球的球员，无法体现多名球员在进球组织过程中的贡献。因此，传统统计数据只能有限地反映球员的参与程度。在本文中，我们使用多元霍克斯过程（MHP）对带时间戳的传球和射门序列进行建模，这些序列构成连续时间网络。MHP 提供了一种分支机制，其中一个事件（传球或射门）可以作为前一个事件的子事件生成，这使我们能够量化每次传球对后续传球或射门事件的贡献。这种方法将功劳分配到进攻序列中的多次传球上，使其能够适用于广泛的场景。基于这一框架，我们……
tldr: 该论文提出利用多元霍克斯过程对足球比赛中带时间戳的传球和射门序列建模，量化每次传球对后续进攻事件的贡献，从而将进球功劳合理分配给进攻组织中的多名球员，弥补了传统助攻统计的局限性。
en_tdlr: This paper uses multivariate Hawkes processes to model timestamped pass and shot sequences in soccer, quantifying each pass's contribution to subsequent attacking events and distributing goal credit across multiple players, thereby overcoming the limitations of traditional assist statistics.
